sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Vessel Hull and Cargo Damage Marine Claims Inspection Survey

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition, substantially harmonized with EU law; the SCSp special limited partnership incorporates common-law limited partnership features through the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union and the People's Republic of China on the reciprocal promotion and protection of investments (signed 6 June 2005, entered into force 1 December 2009)

Convention between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the United States of America for the avoidance of double taxation and the prevention of fiscal evasion (signed 1 April 1996, as amended by the Protocol of 20 May 2009)
Luxembourg-China double taxation agreement (signed 12 March 1994, as modified by the Multilateral Instrument MLI)
EU comprehensive free trade agreements applying to Luxembourg by virtue of EU membership (notably CETA, EU-Japan EPA, EU-Vietnam EVFTA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (consolidated version, as amended most recently by the Law of 20 December 2019 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (UBO Register, administered by the Luxembourg Business Registers); CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 9 December 2004; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (as amended), including the SCSp regime under Articles 944-1 et seq.; Luxembourg administrative and criminal sanctions provisions implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on information accompanying transfers of funds.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (competent authorities, the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit, and AML-obliged entities with a statutory 'legitimate interest' have access; general public access is restricted following the Court of Justice of the EU judgments of 11 November 2022 in Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: SCSp Partnership Agreement (Contrat de Société / Acte Constitutif)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary (authentic deed executed in Luxembourg)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarial authentic deed; no apostille required for the Luxembourg deed itself; certification of conformity at the Luxembourg Chamber of Notaries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Registration / Good Standing of the corporate General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company register of the general partner's country of domicile (e.g., Luxembourg Business Registers for a Luxembourg General Partner)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Hague Convention) issued by the competent authority of the issuing country; no consular legalization required for apostilled jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Judicial Criminal Record Extract (Certificate No. 3) for each director, manager, and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent judicial records authority of the country of residence (Luxembourg Ministry of Justice for residents)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for non-Luxembourg documents; certified translation into French or German where necessary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passports and proof of residential address of all Ultimate Beneficial Owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or administrative authority in the UBO's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus sworn translation into French or German

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming account conduct and absence of adverse AML findings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: House bank of the General Partner and each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letterhead with seal; signature notarized and apostilled under the Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn translation of the Partnership Agreement into French or German (when executed in English)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified or sworn translator admitted in Luxembourg
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Luxembourg sworn translator certification; apostille not required for translations prepared by a Luxembourg sworn translator

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, General Partners, directors, and authorized signatories against the EU consolidated financial sanctions dataset (transposing UN Security Council Resolutions and autonomous EU sanctions), the OFAC SDN list for any USD-denominated wire payment rail, the FATF blacklist and grey-list country-risk references, and domestic Luxembourg asset-freeze measures implemented by the Financial Sanctions Unit of the Ministry of Finance. PEP identification follows the definitions of the Law of 12 November 2004 and FATF Recommendation 12, with enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds documentation, and senior-management approval required upon any PEP or sanctions screening hit. The low-risk determination for a marine claims inspection surveyor remains subject to ongoing transaction monitoring and periodic customer due diligence refresh at least every five years under CSSF Regulation 12-02.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Registre de Commerce et des Societes, electronic portal at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Filings with the RCS are made in French; the statutes and the company name may be expressed in French, German, or English, but any non-French text must be accompanied by a certified translation into French for publication in the RESA (Recueil electronique des societes et associations). The name must be written in Latin script; transliteration into the Latin alphabet is mandatory for any non-Latin script. The legal-form suffix 'Societe en Commandite Speciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp' must appear after the corporate name in all formal documents.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: assurance / insurance or any derivative token such as 'assur' or 'reassurance' — prior written approval of the Commissariat aux Assurances is required before the name may be registered
banque / bank / credit institution or any phonetic equivalent implying deposit-taking — reserved for CSSF-licensed entities
fonds d'investissement / fund / alternative investment fund — reserved for CSSF-registered vehicles
bourse / stock exchange / clearing house — reserved for regulated market infrastructure
etat / gouvernement / commune / ministere — state or municipal designations prohibited unless specifically authorized
trust / fiduciaire / fiduciary / offshore — requires prior approval and may only be used by supervised professionals
societe anonyme, SARL, SCA, SCS or other legal-form tokens inconsistent with the SCSp structure
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The LBR online name availability check is indicative and remains effective for 90 days; formal priority is obtained only upon deposit of the notarial deed and payment of the registration fee. If the RCS rejects a proposed name, the applicant may (1) file a corrective resubmission with supporting consent from any prior right-holder or a revised distinctive token, or (2) lodge an administrative appeal with the Tribunal Administratif of Luxembourg within one month of notification of the rejection, citing the Law of 19 December 2002 and arguing absence of confusion. A parallel complaint may be addressed to the LBR registration division under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 19 December 2002 requesting internal review; external legal counsel should be engaged if the one-month court deadline is at risk.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual mailbox address is not accepted for an SCSp. The registered office must be a physical address in Luxembourg where General Partner decision-making can be evidenced, correspondence of the RCS is received, and statutory books can be inspected. Service providers offering serviced offices are permissible if they provide a dedicated suite, a nameplate, and the appointment of a process agent. For the marine insurance surveyor activity, the registered office must also serve as the centre of day-to-day commercial administration, and any separately maintained operational branch abroad must not undermine Luxembourg commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for this non-financial, low-AML-risk establishment; the annual likelihood of an unannounced on-site inspection by the RCS, the AEDT (fiscal administration), or the Ministry of Economy is estimated below 10% for a compliant entity. The probability increases to moderate (15-30%) if the entity elects VAT registration with reclaims or is later reclassified as a professional of the financial sector for ancillary insurance-services activity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg corporate-services firm or business-plan consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for entity-specific UBO and substance narrative documentation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for ancillary corporate KYC logistics and authorized-signatory documentation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended; Part III on limited partnerships; Article 13-1 et seq. (introduced by law of 23 July 2016) for the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership Agreement (Contrat de Société) – filed electronically with the LBR
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital; capital contributions are freely defined in the partnership agreement and are not subject to statutory escrow account rules unless otherwise agreed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned partners, acting as general and limited partners of the SCSp, hereby adopt the partnership agreement and agree to subscribe to their respective partnership interests as set forth therein. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the partnership be and is hereby fixed at [address], Luxembourg, and the general partner is authorised to register the SCSp with the Luxembourg Business Registers. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [name] be and is hereby appointed as manager (gérant) with full powers to operate the partnership's marine surveying business, open bank accounts, and sign all documents necessary for licensing and compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – online name check via the RCS portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online inquiry to verify the availability of the proposed partnership name against the RCS database. Confirm the name does not conflict with protected trademarks or existing registered entities. If the name is available, proceed to draft the partnership agreement.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or flagged as conflicting, file a new name request with an alternative name that includes the suffix 'SCSp'; re-file within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Signing of Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (optional if all contributions are in cash/kind without immovable property) or partners directly
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement (contrat de société) specifying the contribution, profit-sharing ratios, management powers, and limitations. All partners must sign the agreement. If a contribution in kind or immovable property is involved, the agreement must be notarised before a Luxembourg notary.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity for each partner (passport or ID)
Consent forms for registered office (if not owned)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registry raises objections, amend the agreement and resubmit. Any missing documentation can be completed via publishing an addendum in the RCS filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), RCS e-justice portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the LBR electronic filing system using Luxembourg e-ID/authentication (or a professional registered agent). Upload the signed partnership agreement, statutory declarations, and registered office proof. Pay the lodging fee. Submit the file to the RCS for registration.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of identification for manager/partners
Declaration of non-conviction for the manager (where required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues an incompleteness notice, rectify by resubmitting the missing document in electronic form within 1 month; otherwise re-apply with a new fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of Registration in Official Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS approval, the LBR automatically publishes the incorporation notice in the RESA. No separate submission is required, but the applicant should verify the publication and retain a copy for licensing and bank accounts.
required_dossiers: Copies of published notice (generated by LBR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or erroneous, contact the LBR to request a correction re-publication within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Social Security, and Business Permit Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Revenue Authority (Administration des Contributions Directes – ACD); Joint Social Security Centre (CCSS); Ministry of the Economy (Etablissement Permit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp for corporate income tax, VAT (if annual taxable services exceed EUR 35,000), and business tax. Register the sole manager for social security via CCSS. Apply for an establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) from the Ministry of the Economy if the activity is considered regulated; for marine surveying, submit proof of professional qualifications and liability insurance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the establishment permit is refused, re-apply with updated professional evidence or contest the decision within 3 months before the administrative tribunal (Tribunal administratif).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Directorate for Industry and New Technologies
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Establishment Permit (Autorisation d'Établissement) – Class B (Special Technical Activity) for marine surveying services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – activity is office-based and does not trigger mandatory EIA screening or a full report under the Luxembourg EIA law (Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No direct industrial discharges. Indoor occupational exposure should comply with the Labour Code (Code du Travail) and general waste segregation rules. Any incidental chemical use (e.g., ultrasonic testing fluids) must be disposed via certified waste handlers under the Waste Management Law (Law of 21 March 2012).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) for the registered office; structural load inspection and workplace safety clearance issued by the Labour and Mines Inspectorate (ITM) confirming compliance with occupational safety standards and accessibility for professional survey equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) — Luxembourg Inland Revenue — for corporate income tax, net wealth tax and withholding taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — for VAT (TVA), registration duties and indirect taxes; Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) — for commercial registration. Digital filing portals: MyGuichet.lu (guichet.lu) and the AEDT eTVA/e-filing platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned SCSp (fiscally transparent partnership): (1) obtain the LBR matricule (12-digit business registration number) via MyGuichet.lu where the SCSp maintains a Luxembourg registered office or establishment; (2) file VAT registration application Form 1024 with the AEDT to obtain the Luxembourg national VAT ID — mandatory from the first taxable supply in Luxembourg for non-established suppliers, with no turnover threshold, and appointment of an approved Luxembourg VAT representative required if the SCSp is established outside the EU; (3) apply to the ACD for a Luxembourg tax identification number (TIN) for direct tax filings using the taxpayer registration procedure with the ACD's central taxpayer identification service; partners report their distributive shares using their own TINs; the official legal entity identifier is the LBR matricule for non-tax administrative filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — the SCSp is a fiscal-transparent partnership (sans personnalité juridique) for Luxembourg income tax and net wealth tax purposes; profits pass through to partners and are taxable at partner level (no CIT or net wealth tax at the SCSp level), subject to ATAD hybrid-mismatch and reverse-hybrid anti-abuse rules; for VAT, the SCSp is treated as a separate taxable person in respect of its economic activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg law has no general check-the-box regime; fiscal transparency is the statutory default of the SCSp. Available elections: (i) VAT: the SCSp may elect to be a VAT taxable person and may join a VAT group (assujetti unique) under Article 61 of the VAT Law; (ii) US federal tax: the SCSp may file an IRS Form 8832 check-the-box election to be classified as a corporation or as a partnership for US purposes; (iii) ATAD reverse-hybrid rule (Law of 21 December 2019): an SCSp controlled by taxpayers in a non-EU jurisdiction that treats it as a taxable entity is recharacterised as a Luxembourg taxable entity and loses pass-through treatment; (iv) commercial/accounting: the partnership deed may govern profit allocation and fiduciary arrangements, and cross-border PE/profit attribution elections may be available under applicable tax treaties.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / TVA) — Luxembourg national VAT administered by the AEDT
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover (franchise de TVA) for resident small businesses; zero threshold for non-resident/non-established suppliers — VAT registration is required from the first taxable supply in Luxembourg; intra-EU distance sales of goods subject to the EUR 10,000 EU-wide distance-selling threshold under OSS/IOSS rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping or general B2B e-invoicing mandate in Luxembourg as of the current framework. Mandatory e-invoicing applies only to B2G supplies to Luxembourg public entities (PEPPOL/UBL format routed via MyGuichet.lu/Peppol). VAT returns and EC sales lists must be filed electronically through the AEDT's eTVA portal; API-based filing is available for large taxpayers. Taxpayers must retain a full audit trail for the statutory 10-year record-keeping period. The EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) reform will introduce mandatory B2B e-invoicing for intra-EU supplies once implemented.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rate (0%) applies to: (i) goods physically exported from Luxembourg to destinations outside the EU, subject to proof of export within the legal time limits; (ii) services directly connected with international transport of goods or with exports, including marine cargo surveying and vessel hull damage inspection services supplied to non-EU insurers/underwriters, provided the B2B place-of-supply rules locate the supply outside Luxembourg (customer outside the EU), resulting in zero Luxembourg VAT with the right to deduct input VAT; (iii) services qualifying under Articles 44 and 46 of the Luxembourg VAT Law for international trade. The marine surveyor must hold documentary evidence of the customer's non-EU status (valid VAT registration certificate or equivalent) and of the actual cross-border use or physical export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (formal/ECS export declaration accepted by Luxembourg customs authorities)
Bill of Lading (or CMR/AWB multimodal transport document) evidencing physical departure from the EU
Inward remittance certificate / bank wire confirmation (SWIFT or SEPA) evidencing payment by the non-EU contractual counterparty
Signed marine survey and inspection service contract with the non-EU insurer or underwriter
Survey report and claim inspection certificate identifying the vessel/cargo, place of survey, consignee and insurer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and Luxembourg customs jointly audit export zero-rating claims. Missing or inconsistent export, transport or FX-repatriation documentation within the 180-day evidence window triggers retrospective reversal of the 0% rate, assessment of unpaid VAT at 17%, default interest of 0.6% per month (Article 36 of the VAT Law), and administrative penalties under Article 43 of the VAT Law (fine of EUR 250–10,000 per offence; higher fines for serious irregularities). Fraudulent or abusive claims — false declarations, forged bills of lading, artificial routing schemes, or sham non-EU counterparties — constitute tax fraud punishable under Luxembourg criminal tax law with imprisonment (up to 5 years), fines of up to EUR 50,000, publication of the judgment, and debarment from tax clearance certificates. The limitation period extends to 5 years (10 years in fraud cases), and EU mutual assistance, DAC6 exchange and joint cross-border customs/VAT controls enable retrospective clawbacks.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) and Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg does not operate exchange controls and applies the EU free movement of capital under Article 63 TFEU. Current-account payments, including cross-border marine survey fees and reinsurance disbursements, and capital-account flows, including partner contributions, advances, and liquidation distributions, are fully convertible into EUR, USD, GBP, and other freely tradable currencies. No central bank conversion permit, transfer approval, or profit-remittance authorization is required for the SCSp. Profit distribution is subject to no exchange-control hurdle, but a Luxembourg paying bank will require documented distributable reserves, partner approval formalities, and standard AML/KYC confirmation of final beneficial owners. The practical compliance friction is not convertibility but evidentiary proof of source of funds and underlying economic substance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no mandatory surrender, repatriation timeline, or conversion ratio for export proceeds, including earnings from marine cargo and vessel hull survey services supplied to foreign insurers and underwriters. Export proceeds may be retained in EUR or foreign currency in the SCSp's bank accounts, freely reinvested, or converted in the spot or forward market. BCL statistics-reporting requirements may apply to resident entities for cross-border service receipts and capital flows, but such statistical reporting is not a repatriation or conversion control.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (survey fee collection, disbursements, and FX settlement)
Capital Escrow Account (inward partner capital contributions)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, Luxembourg (BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR SEPA settlement and regulatory trust flows)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: LOW as the primary treasury rail, MEDIUM as a supplemental outward-payment channel. An offshore digital EMI that is not authorized in the EEA cannot lawfully provide payment services to a Luxembourg-resident SCSp under the Payment Services Directive (EU) 2015/2366 and the Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004, as amended. An EEA-licensed EMI may passport into Luxembourg through the CSSF/BCL notification regime, but the bank will subject the SCSp to full CDD and may decline to treat the EMI as the main settlement account because of corporate treasury, waiver, and closing-risk concerns. For low-value 'Underwriter_Wire' and Wise-type supplier reimbursements, an EEA-authorized EMI can be a practical supplementary rail after the primary Luxembourg bank account is active and the treasury policy explicitly defines permissible EMI transaction limits and reconciliation controls.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the practical default for a non-resident-owned SCSp seeking first-time account opening. Luxembourg AML legislation and CSSF regulations do not impose a single statutory in-person interview rule, but the risk-based approach, combined with the SCSp's lack of legal personality and reliance on non-resident limited partners, makes Luxembourg banks require at least one authorized managing partner or officer to attend a face-to-face KYC/origin meeting, either at the bank's offices, at an acceptable Luxembourg notary, or through a video-conference interview vetted by the bank. Pure remote onboarding without an existing bank relationship is generally not available for an offshore SCSp; where remote opening is exceptionally permitted, the bank will require qualified electronic signature, a valid passport, proof of residence, notarized or apostilled partnership deed, and a live or recorded interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident, non-EU ultimate beneficial owners controlling the SCSp through an unincorporated Luxembourg partnership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current extract from the Luxembourg register of beneficial owners (RBE), complete partnership agreement and side letters, signed UBO declaration, full corporate ownership chart, passport copies, apostilled/notarized proof of address, bank reference from the UBO's home institution, source of wealth and source of funds reports, and a legal opinion confirming the entity operates solely as a marine surveying partnership and not as a regulated insurance company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border collections of marine survey fees from insurers and rapid on-payment to overseas subcontractors, repair yards, and loss adjusters.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML/CTF policies and procedures manual, risk-based CDD file of all material counterparties, expected-jurisdiction list, executed engagement letters and marine survey reports, itemized invoices corresponding to underwriter wire receipts, underlying trade contracts for each outbound disbursement, and periodic transaction monitoring reports prepared by the compliance function.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital contributions or periodic funding received from offshore jurisdictions through structured holding companies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled partnership agreement, capital calls and partner minutes, contributing partner bank statements, proof of legality of funds, tax clearance certificates from relevant residence jurisdictions, substance documentation (office lease, service-provider agreement, payroll records, professional indemnity insurance), RBE filings, and an independent tax counsel comfort letter on Luxembourg tax transparency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Licensed-status ambiguity for the marine-insurance-surveyor activity, especially potential classification as claims management or insurance distribution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory license or authorization certificate where required by Luxembourg law, engagement letters disclaiming insurance distribution and claims settlement authority, professional credentials of the surveyors, professional indemnity insurance policy, written scope-of-services matrix, and a regulatory status memo analyzing applicability of the Luxembourg Law of 7 December 2018 on insurance distribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outward payments to beneficiaries, suppliers, or claimant representatives in high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions in connection with marine loss assessments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction-specific compliance memorandum, underlying insurance or cargo claim contract, detailed survey assessment report, verified beneficiary due diligence, sanctions screening results against UN, EU, and OFAC lists, source of funds documentation from the remitting insurer, payment route justification, and the AML compliance officer's approval record.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital contributions should be routed over SWIFT MT103 for direct remittances from a partner or parent treasury, or over MT202 for interbank funding where the remitter is a financial institution. Euro contributions from an EEA partner may use a SEPA Credit Transfer to the SCSp's Luxembourg IBAN. The remittance narrative must identify the commercial purpose as 'Capital contribution to Luxembourg SCSp', 'Subscription of partnership interests', or 'Partner advance per partnership agreement'. Where a SWIFT purpose code is required, the sender should apply category B301 for contributions to corporate capital and B304 for intra-group partner loans; the receiving bank will require a pre-funded Capital Escrow Account, a copy of the capital call, RBE registration evidence, notarized partnership documents, and completion of partner KYC before the funds can be released to the operational account. The BCL's balance-of-payments statistics reporting must capture the transaction, but no regulatory pre-approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rails for outbound trade and operational disbursements are SWIFT MT103 for direct invoice settlements and reimburseable survey expenses, SWIFT MT202/COV for USD bank-to-bank settlement chains, SEPA Credit Transfers in EUR for payments within the European Economic Area, and documentary commercial letters of credit issued or confirmed under UCP600 when the transaction involves procurement of vessel spares, repair services, or equipment subject to LC terms. For low-value, non-bankable counterparty payments, an EEA-authorized EMI such as Wise Business may be used after the principal Luxembourg bank account is operational, subject to a documented treasury policy limiting EMI exposure and requiring complete underlying invoice matching. The bank will require a signed disbursement instruction from the authorized manager, underlying contract or invoice, sanctions screening of the payee, and, where applicable, evidence that the payee is the true beneficial owner of the settlement amount.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable FX forwards denominated in EUR, USD, GBP, and other G10 currencies to hedge underwriter premium receipts and claims disbursements.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible or restricted-deliverable currencies where the bank and client establish a genuine commercial exposure and the transaction complies with EMIR and CSSF hedging eligibility standards.
Cross-currency swaps for longer-tenor partner advances, capital subscription obligations, or liability-driven matches between the SCSp's foreign-currency receivables and liquidity commitments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation declaration to the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March; filing window opens on 1 January of the same year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to EUR 5,000; repeated failure can trigger removal/strike-off from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual collective partnership income tax return (déclaration collective de revenus) for the fiscally transparent SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 May; if filed electronically via a registered tax advisor, the extended deadline is the following 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest and penalties up to 10% of the tax at stake; administrative fine in case of non-response to formal notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory accounts filing (if the SCSp exceeds the size thresholds or if the constitutive agreement imposes it)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the financial year end; 31 July for calendar-year partnerships
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of up to EUR 5,000; possibility of criminal prosecution for reckless non-filing and judicial strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory if two of three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, net turnover above EUR 8.8 million, and average staff headcount above 50. For an SCSp, audit is also required if the agreement of partners mandates it or if it forms part of a regulated financial group.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Lux GAAP) based on the Law of 11 May 2007 on annual accounts; IFRS as adopted by the EU permitted for consolidated and certain voluntary scenarios.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No stand-alone annual UBO declaration due in Luxembourg; UBO register data must be filed with the Luxembourg Business Registers within one month of any qualifying change in shareholding/ownership, and the annual RCS declaration is used to confirm the underlying registered data. For a shareholding transfer, the updated UBO identification must be filed electronically within the same one-month window.
